messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: ALERT: Paging oncall for P1 - KMS API errors detected affecting token signing and service startup in multiple regions. See logs/stack traces. Pager: @alice.m :rotating_light:

alice.m: I'm on it. getting initial scope. which KMS are we seeing errors to? gcp-us-east4 or aws-kms?

ben.platform: seeing increased latency and 5xx from GCP KMS in us-east4 and europe-west1. Clients trying to fetch DEK at startup hit timeouts and fail preflight, lots of crashes in dedicated pods.

charlie.sre: confirming. trends: spikes starting ~1790004800, RTT to KMS API jumped from ~120ms to 4-7s with intermittent 502s. Retries exhausted at client side and signing returns 504.

devon-support: customer-facing queue flagged ~8 high-visibility users reporting app boot failures since ~07:08 UTC. Notified CSMs.

alice.m: mitigations: (1) increase KMS client timeout and retries for a rolling restart window? (2) enable local in-memory fallback keys for non-prod? (3) route to secondary KMS region if possible? thoughts?

ben.platform: quick wins: bump client retry backoff, enable shorter circuit-breaker so we fail-fast to avoid request pileup, and temporarily switch signing to standby key store for non-sensitive onboarding traffic. For Dedicated customers we need opt-in.

emily-obs: dashboard: https://obs.redwood.internal/d/keys/kms-latency — alert volume correlates with a vendor-side incident: GCP KMS incident reported region-wide. I'm attaching sample error from logs:

```
2026-03-15T07:09:21Z ERROR signing: kms: request failed: Status=502 Body="Bad Gateway" remote="kms.googleapis.com" attempt=2
2026-03-15T07:09:25Z WARN  startup: could not fetch DEK: context deadline exceeded
```

charlie.sre: I've opened a support ticket with Google (INC-987654). They acknowledged elevated API latency in the region and are investigating. ETA unknown.

alice.m: Immediate runbook actions I'm executing now:
- set service-level circuit-breaker to 500ms for KMS calls (to fail fast)
- increase retries with exponential backoff up to 2s (to smooth spikes)
- toggle feature-flag to allow use of cached DEKs for 10m grace period during startup
- enable fallback signing path to our HSM proxy in us-central (limited capacity)

ben.platform: rolling config change in progress. patch:

```yaml
kms:
  timeout_ms: 500
  max_retries: 3
  retry_backoff_ms: 200
  fallback_cache_ttl: 600
```

devon-support: notif sent to affected customers: "We're investigating elevated latency to a cloud KMS provider causing some startup failures. We're applying mitigations; if you see errors please escalate to support."

alice.m: @charlie.sre when you have a link to the vendor incident, drop it here so we can track public status. Also flagging this for oncall handoff at 07:30 UTC. I'll hand to @ben.platform if still active.

charlie.sre: vendor link: https://status.cloud.google.com/incident/kms/2026-03-15 — updated: investigating.

pagerduty-bot: Incident page created: https://pd.redwood.internal/incidents/2026-03-15-kms-latency. Severity: P1. Coordinator: alice.m.

emily-obs: Metrics during mitigation: KMS call error rate down from 12% -> 4% after circuit-breaker and retry tweaks. Startup failure rate for new pods reduced by ~70%.

ben.platform: handing oncall to @charlie.sre at 07:30 UTC for next hour. I'll keep available for escalations. Leaving runbook note: if vendor resolves, we need to rollback circuit-breaker and remove fallback in a controlled canary.

alice.m: Handoff ack. Summary for next responder:
- Impact: startup failures and signing errors for new containers in us-east4 & europe-west1; some production requests saw increased latency but no broad data loss.
- Mitigations applied: client circuit-breaker, increased retries, cached DEK fallback TTL 10m, HSM proxy fallback in us-central for limited traffic.
- Vendor: GCP KMS investigating (INC-987654).
- Customers: ~8 dedicated customers with visible errors; support notified.

charlie.sre: continuing to monitor. If vendor posts fix, we'll: (1) revert circuit-breaker/timeouts in canary, (2) disable cached-DEK fallback after 2 successful canary restarts, (3) run post-incident key-integrity checks.

devon-support: logging this to the incident doc and aligning CSM comms.

alice.m: Thanks team. Leaving channel for handoff. If anything spikes, ping me and I'll jump back. :white_check_mark:

incident-bot: Note: oncall handoff recorded. Next oncall: charlie.sre at 07:30 UTC. Postmortem owner requested.

charlie.sre: grabbing postmortem. I'll include timeline, root cause (vendor KMS API latency), mitigations and follow-ups: (a) add region failover for KMS calls, (b) add client-side smoother backoff jitter, (c) add automated degraded-mode circuit-breaker with safe defaults.

pagerduty-bot: PagerDuty alert resolved for initial surge; monitoring remains open.

emily-obs: leaving final note: observed residual 1% error rate for 30m. Recommend waiting 1h after vendor clear before rolling back fallbacks.

charlie.sre: acknowledged. I'll keep the incident open until vendor declares root cause fixed and we've validated key integrity across regions.

devon-support: I'll gather impacted customer list and attach to the incident doc.

alice.m: end of thread for now. Rapid, pragmatic mitigations reduced customer impact and kept most traffic healthy. We'll follow-up with full postmortem and communications. :bow:
